name: Purchase materials and services
summary: Purchasing turns approved requisitions from maintenance, stores replenishment, outages and projects into purchase orders and follows them until the goods arrive. A budget holder approves the requisition, a buyer checks it, releases it against a contract or gets quotes, creates the PO and has it approved when it is above the buyer's limit, then chases the supplier's confirmation and expedites critical items until stores receive them. Delays come from unclear specifications, slow approvers, suppliers that take days to quote, single-source OEM parts with long lead times, and price or quantity mismatches that block the invoice.

baseline.org_archetype: A central procurement team of about 20 serving an Alberta generator's gas, hydro, wind, mine and project groups from one ERP, with buyers organised by material group.
baseline.notes: No e-sourcing or supplier portal is assumed; quotes and acknowledgements travel by email. COVID-19 lengthened lead times in 2021-2022.

trigger: A purchase requisition is submitted in the ERP by a planner, storekeeper, engineer or project manager.
end_state: The goods or services are received against the PO and the invoice can be matched, or the requisition is rejected.

volume.seasonality: Peaks in the two to three months before each spring and fall outage season, when outage material lists are bought.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Outage material purchases run ahead of the outage seasons; the multiplier is an estimate below the organisation file's because routine and project buying continue at the normal rate.
Kept at the organisation file's estimate: 12 buyers at about 60 to 80 POs each a month. No published PO count for the company.
Org file lists 12 buyers; the rest of their time goes to service orders, supplier meetings and outage material lists. Estimate.
Commercial review share of 6 contract specialists; estimate.
PO release above buyer limits; estimate.
Stands for all budget-holder approvers (thermal, hydro, wind, outage and project leads); estimate.
Stands for all requesters answering buyer queries; estimate.

systems.name: ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)
Document management and engineering drawings repository

steps.name: Approve purchase requisition
steps.description: The budget holder for the requesting area, most often a maintenance supervisor, gets an ERP workflow email, opens the requisition, checks that the work is needed and charged to the right work order or cost centre, and approves or rejects it within their spending limit.

control.basis: Corporate delegation of authority: spending limits by role and value

evidence.note: Requisition approval under a delegation of authority is standard in listed companies; the waits are estimates for an office-hours approver who spends much of the day in the plant.

steps.name: Route requisition to buyer queue
steps.description: The ERP assigns the approved requisition to a purchasing group by material group and plant, and it appears in that buyer's open requisition list overnight or at once, depending on the release setting.

steps.name: Review requisition for completeness
steps.description: The buyer opens the requisition and checks the description, OEM part number, quantity, required date, delivery point and account. Unclear items go back to the requester; urgent breakdown items are bought at once by phone.

error.defect_description: Unclear specification passed on to suppliers.

next.condition: emergency: buy at once from a known supplier

evidence.note: Shares are estimates; Reliabilityweb (rweb_store) reports that stock-outs drive many reactive emergency purchases in typical MRO operations.

steps.name: Answer buyer query on specification
steps.description: The planner or engineer who raised the requisition looks up the OEM manual, nameplate photo or drawing, corrects the part number or description, and replies to the buyer by email or by editing the requisition.

steps.name: Check contracts, catalogues and approved suppliers
steps.description: The buyer searches the ERP for outline agreements and info records, the contract repository for master supply or service agreements, and the approved supplier list, to decide whether the item can be released against a contract, must go to the OEM, or needs quotes.

error.defect_description: Existing contract missed, so the item is bought at a higher spot price.

next.condition: release against an existing agreement or catalogue price
single source: OEM or proprietary part

evidence.note: Vendor research cited there puts duplicate purchases at 5 to 7 percent of spend; source shares here are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Justify single source and request OEM quote
steps.description: For proprietary turbine, boiler or control system parts, the buyer writes a short single-source justification, attaches it to the requisition and emails the OEM or its authorised distributor for price and lead time.

control.basis: Procurement policy: written justification for single-source purchases above the quote threshold

steps.name: Send request for quotation
steps.description: The buyer picks two or three suppliers from the approved list and emails a request for quotation with the specification, quantity, required date and terms, or issues it from the ERP.

error.defect_description: RFQ sent with the wrong revision or quantity.

steps.name: Suppliers prepare quotes
steps.description: Suppliers price the request and reply by email; the buyer waits for the quote deadline, chasing slow responders. Western Canadian distributors usually answer in days, OEMs in weeks.

steps.name: Compare quotes and select supplier
steps.description: The buyer tabulates price, lead time, freight and commercial exceptions in a spreadsheet, checks technical compliance with the requester where needed, and selects the supplier. High-value or services awards go to contract review.

error.defect_description: Lower price picked with a lead time that misses the need date.

next.condition: high value or services: contract review

steps.name: Review commercial terms and supplier qualification
steps.description: For high-value purchases and on-site services the contract specialist checks the terms and conditions, insurance, and contractor safety prequalification, negotiates exceptions and sets up the supplier in the ERP if it is new.

control.basis: Procurement policy: contract review and contractor safety prequalification above value thresholds

steps.name: Create purchase order
steps.description: The buyer converts the requisition into a purchase order in the ERP, re-keys the quoted price, delivery date, freight terms and supplier reference from the quote, and attaches the quote and any justification.

error.defect_description: Wrong price, unit of measure or delivery address keyed.

steps.name: Approve purchase order above buyer limit
steps.description: The supply chain manager (or an executive for the largest orders) reviews the PO value, supplier, sourcing method and justification in the ERP release workflow and releases it or sends it back.

control.basis: Corporate delegation of authority: spending limits by role and value; buyer cannot release own PO above limit

steps.name: Send purchase order to supplier
steps.description: The ERP output run emails the released purchase order as a PDF to the supplier's order address and posts a commitment against the work order or cost centre.

steps.name: Supplier acknowledges order
steps.description: The supplier confirms the order, price and delivery date by email or returns a signed acknowledgement; many do not reply unless chased.

steps.name: Chase acknowledgement or negotiate date
steps.description: The buyer phones or emails the supplier for a confirmed ship date and, if it misses the need date, asks for partial or expedited shipment or looks for an alternative source with the requester.

steps.name: Update promised date and tell requester
steps.description: The buyer enters the confirmed delivery date in the PO and emails the planner if it affects the scheduled work, so the work order can be rescheduled.

error.defect_description: Promised date not updated, so planners schedule against a wrong date.

steps.name: Distributor ships from stock
steps.description: The supplier picks from stock or manufactures the item and ships it by courier or truck to the plant warehouse. Distributor stock from Edmonton or Calgary arrives in days to two weeks.

evidence.note: The 2021 AIF names supply chain disruption and the ability to secure equipment as a risk; lead-time range for stocked items (1 to 14 days, mode 3) is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Expedite critical or late order
steps.description: For outage and breakdown items the buyer calls the supplier weekly, asks for shop progress, arranges premium freight or partial shipments, and reports status at the outage or plant planning meeting.

evidence.note: Expediting share and effort are estimates; the organisation file names long-lead single-source parts for older units.

steps.name: OEM or fabricator makes and ships the item
steps.description: Made-to-order and proprietary parts, such as valve internals, pump impellers, turbine seals and control cards for the older units, are manufactured or pulled from the OEM's global stock and shipped, often across the border with customs clearance.

evidence.note: Supply chain disruption and securing equipment are named risks in the 2021 AIF; the lead-time range (1 week to 3 months, mode 3 weeks) is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Goods receipt updates the order
steps.description: Stores post the goods receipt against the PO when the delivery is checked in, which updates the open quantity, the commitment and the receipt date the buyer sees. Discrepancies come back to the buyer.

next.condition: invoice blocked for price or quantity

evidence.note: Receipt itself is done in scm-manage-stores; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Resolve receiving discrepancy with supplier
steps.description: When stores report a short, damaged or wrong item, the buyer contacts the supplier, arranges a return authorisation and a replacement or credit, and keeps the PO line open.

steps.name: Resolve invoice price or quantity block
steps.description: Accounts payable report that the invoice fails the three-way match; the buyer compares PO, receipt and invoice, gets a credit note or corrects the PO price, and releases the block.

control.basis: Three-way match of PO, goods receipt and invoice under internal control over financial reporting

exceptions.name: Emergency purchase
exceptions.description: A breakdown item is bought at once by phone from a known supplier, skipping quotes.

exceptions.name: Specification query
exceptions.description: The buyer cannot source from the description and asks the requester to clarify.

exceptions.name: Single-source OEM part
exceptions.description: Proprietary parts need a justification and an OEM quote, often with long lead times.

exceptions.name: Critical or late order expedited
exceptions.description: Made-to-order and OEM items are followed up weekly until shipped.

exceptions.name: Invoice block
exceptions.description: Price or quantity differs between PO, receipt and invoice.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from requisition submitted to goods received
benchmarks.population: MRO and project purchases at a mid-size generator, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about a week from requisition to PO when quotes are needed and one to three weeks of supplier lead time for distributor stock, with OEM parts in the tail. APQC's requisition-to-PO measure could not be opened (access refused), so it is not used.

pain_points.description: Requisitions with vague descriptions or no OEM part number bounce between buyer and requester before they can be quoted.
Stock-outs and unplanned breakdowns turn into emergency purchases at spot prices without competition.
Single-source OEM parts for the older converted units have long and uncertain lead times, and supply chain disruption in 2021-2022 made them longer.

evidence.note: Supply chain disruption named as a risk; lead times are estimates.

pain_points.description: Approvals wait for supervisors and managers who are in the plant or in meetings.
Keying errors in PO prices and units block invoices later and pull buyers into accounts payable queries.

sources.title: Reliability vs the capricious MRO storeroom
sources.supports: Undated practitioner article on typical MRO storerooms: fill rates of stocked SKUs under 80 percent (out of stock 20 percent of the time); only 50 to 70 percent of planned work orders are filled from stores and 30 to 50 percent cause reactive, emergency purchases; inaccurate inventory quantities disrupt reservations; planners, purchasing and engineers stop their work to chase parts.

sources.title: MRO and spare parts inventory statistics: stockouts, accuracy, costs
sources.supports: Undated review. Practitioners commonly target 95 to 98 percent inventory record accuracy (a management target, not a measured average); no large-scale audit of MRO storeroom record accuracy was found; vendor research puts duplicate purchases at 5 to 7 percent of spend; a 2025 vendor survey found 22 percent of MRO inventory unused for more than five years and about 66 percent of manufacturers managing MRO in the ERP alone.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Forward-looking risk list names disruptions to supply chains, including the ability to secure necessary equipment, and equipment failure and the ability to complete repairs cost-effectively; the partner (Heartland) operates and maintains the Sheerness units; Sundance 4 stopped firing coal from January 1, 2022; Highvale mining ended at the end of 2021; many employees have more than 20 years of service.

assumptions: The maintenance supervisor stands in for every budget-holder approver and the maintenance planner for every requester, because those are the largest group; hydro, wind, outage and project approvers follow the same step.
Requisitions from hydro maintenance and wind troubleshooting are included (14 percent) although the organisation file routes those processes only to stores.
The process ends at goods receipt; receiving work is counted in gen-scm-manage-stores and invoice matching in fin-pay-suppliers, except the buyer's work on blocked invoices (s21).
Service orders for contractors follow the same steps; larger contracts belong to scm-contractor-management.

Requisition-to-PO time in this model (median about a week when quotes are needed) is longer than cross-industry figures for simple catalogue buys because it includes quote waits; no benchmark page that states such figures could be opened.
